title: WPA rules: daily practice, three-hour shifts and ending
summary: Musicians had to report daily and were sent to three-hour jobs; Morris played nights with Rena, was caught, and went back to the riverfront.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: They noticed, Dave, did you have to report every day and practice?

Every day, yes. Practice every day. Every day, every day. And when you'd miss, that was a bad mock against you. They didn't want to know what's the trouble. If you get sick or something, you had to let them know.
Did you ever have a parade that you had to play or concert? What did they do?
Oh, yeah. We used to have to play. Everybody's name was Check and Call. Just like you call them roll. Your name had to be Check and Call.
Did they have any small group for a dance band, too?
Well, they used to split them up.
Split them up there. What happened?

You see, now, I used to play at night down there by the Portland and St. Claude down there by the 5th precinct. I was playing there with Renier at night. See? Well, somehow or another, they found it out.
You were getting paid then for the other job, too.

Yeah, I was getting paid, yeah. But they found it out, well, that's why they stopped knocking you off at 2 o'clock in the day. And they start, when you come in the morning and make a three hour, and you go back 6 and 7 o'clock and 8 o'clock at night and make the other three hour. That's keep you from going on any job. You couldn't get a band. Because all the musicians was in the PWA there, and you couldn't hire a band not funny, not easy. So that was something, wasn't it? Them people found a way somehow or another to bust you up. Sometimes they'd send maybe but 8 in this place or 8 o'clock tonight or tomorrow night. And they'd send anybody to eat in that place or 10 in this place or 20 in that place or 15 in that. And you had to go to all them different places why they send you. All them different streets. I guess I done been all over this town. I wouldn't know half the way why they go now. Yeah. And they had to do that.
Did you play for a dance then? They'd send you out for a dance or something.
Yes, a dance. Three hours. You wouldn't play any more than three hours. No, sir. And they couldn't keep you no longer than that. That's the orders.
Oh, I see, yeah.
They have that paper. When they're three hours up, you're gone. They knock you off.
Well, there's something.
And they had a man there to take your timekeeper to take your time? No. Yes, sir. You know.
Somebody said they finally broke up that whole project and no more music, and they sent them out to dig ditches at the city park or something. Do you remember?
Well, no, sir. Well, me, I didn't dig no more.
There's a lake there where they...

I didn't do no digging at all. Because when it got slack and they had to break up and different things, I went on back on the riverfront. I went on back down by the Portland Barcage and went on back to work.
